incumbent_comparison: Better than display_cabinet-v001: two transparent framed doors, brass handles, hinge details, crown and base molding now read in the actual production captures, and the internal shelves remain visible behind the glass.

observations.art_direction_fit: The warm case and subtle brass fit the room's furniture style and maintain a low-poly silhouette.
observations.close_up_quality: The front three-quarter capture resolves the framed doors and visible shelving; the room's separate collectible blocks are seen above the cabinet in their unchanged RoomDefinition positions.
observations.gameplay_readability: The cabinet is easy to distinguish from the separate room collectibles and other tall furniture; no gameplay object definition changed.
observations.geometric_detail: Captured details include two framed glass doors, mullions, cross rails, brass handles, hinge hardware, three internal shelves, and finished moldings.
observations.material_realism: Warm textured wood and lightly tinted transparent glass are visually distinct; the interior shelves remain visible through the doors.
observations.proportion: The tall, narrow cabinet fits its wall placement and reads as a freestanding case.
observations.scale_fidelity: Godot technical bounds pass against the 33 x 76 x 18-inch target, and the production resolver normalizes to the existing RoomDefinition dimensions.
observations.semantic_recognizability: The production close views clearly show a tall wood and glass display cabinet with two doors and internal shelves.
observations.silhouette_quality: The full-height case, crown, base, and framed glass front create a recognizable display cabinet shape.
observations.surface_variation: Wood case, dark trim, brass fittings, transparent glass, and interior shelf surfaces form a varied but cohesive palette.
observations.technical_integration: The native scene passes Godot validation and the production resolver loads display_cabinet-v002 for all six standardized captures without fallback.
